props.doc: Pekko HTTP: nested and conjoined verbs, a composed multi-segment prefix, and a prefix held in a value that cannot be resolved without evaluating Scala.

A MIXIN, not an abstraction: a self-type and a body of concrete definitions, with no abstract member anywhere. This is the ordinary way to compose a Scala service, and counting it as an abstraction reported a package of these as "useless". Its `abstract=false` in the golden is the assertion.
A timer, not a web server. `path` is an ordinary method name, and matching the Pekko directive without the routing import produced routes from this shape.
Outbound calls the cross-repo linker can join to whoever serves them, plus one third-party call that must NOT read as an unresolved internal edge.
A forum has topics. None of them are Kafka topics, and this file's ABSENCE from the storage facts is the assertion — a phantom topic would invent cross-repo coupling by name ownership.

An anonymous class is where Scala puts implementations, and its body was dropped whole before v185 — so a method whose only call site lives in one read as dead. Both spellings are here: Scala 3's braceless `new:` and the classic `new T { }`.

Called WITHOUT parentheses, which Scala's uniform access principle permits for a parameterless method. The grammar reports it as a field access, so before v186 it produced no edge and `ready` read as dead code.
http4s: the endpoint lives in a pattern rather than in calls.
The direct I/O sink: `db.run` is the point every Slick query reaches the database, and the receiver is what makes the generic method name qualify.
Phase 2 surface: the loop model, the call graph, and the I/O closure.
Nested collection combinators compound; `synchronized` is not a loop.
Reaches the database only through two wrapper hops — performs_io must propagate all the way here for the analyzer to see the N+1 above.
A real iteration: `load` runs once per id, so it is an N+1 candidate.
A monadic bind: `enrich` runs exactly once. Counting this as a loop is what would put an N+1 on every effectful method in a Scala codebase.
The generator is evaluated once, so `fetchIds` is not per-iteration work.
Cross-module resolution: `Base` is declared in another sbt project, and `LegacyId` in another LANGUAGE in that project. Both must resolve internal.
Scala 3 syntax: braceless bodies, enum, given, extension.
A real abstraction, for contrast: one member declared and not implemented.
A topic constant beside a real broker import: the asynchronous coupling a call graph structurally cannot see.

Directory is app/src/main/scala/weird; package is com.example.renamed. The fact NAME is directory-anchored, the fqn follows the package, and the `extends Base` edge resolves through the import either way.
A Java type in the same package as the Scala sources, so the cross-language package index is exercised: app's Scala import of it must resolve as internal.
A trait becomes an interface; a case class carries its marker.

A shipped fixture LIBRARY: production code living under a directory named `test`. zio-test is the real case this pins — its presence in the golden is the assertion that the Scala test globs scope to the sbt source set.
